findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present during today’s visit. The PIC’s certification expired on 8/10/2026. The PIC has plans to take the exam at the District 186 Office. Ensure there is a CFPM present prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

The inspector observed the triple sink to be missing its sealant at the back of the sink. The sink needs to be sealed to the wall to prevent water and microbial accumulation. Ensure this repair is complete prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 
Five packages of ham were observed to have holes in them when removed from freezer and thawing method. The manager noticed holes in ham packages this morning, when the sheet pan used during thawing, had ham juice on it. Mor holes were observed after ham was removed from thawing in water and water was running out of the ham packages. All together 25 pounds of ham were discarded due to packaging that was not intact. Some holes were as large as a pencil eraser while others were smaller but still exposed the food inside to potential contamination. This is the first time that this kitchen has used this ham product. Normally they use turkey ham and have not had any previous issue with packaging that is not intact.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade had some debris on the blade, and a chunk of food debris was observed on the vertical bar beneath the blade. Can opener had not been used since the start of operations today and was set aside at the 3 part sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Staff noted the can opener is used maybe twice a week and is always cleaned and sanitized after use. Ensure that any other persons with access to the can opener know to properly clean and sanitize it or at minimum set it aside for cleaning after use. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: The wiping cloth bucket has 0ppm of quat. The wiping cloth bucket was remade and now tests at 200ppm of quat. Watch buckets and keep solutions clean and at the proper concentrations. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed towels in the bottom of the clean utensil holder. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Make certain that the non food contact surfaces are smooth and cleansable. Not absorbent. Towels were removed.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed ham portions in the upright cooler at an internal temperature of between 52F and 54F. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while in storage, display and service. The ham portions have been discarded.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Unlabeled portions of cooling pasta salad were observed inside cooler. Trays were not labeled with date and/or time. Labeling was discussed with Manager.
Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - Box of single service items (plastic portion container lids) observed on the floor by storage shelves. Staff noted delivery was received on 9/18. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor. Provide a means to keep single service items up off the floor when space is not yet available on shelves. Acceptable storage would include placing up on a chair, an inverted milk crate, or on top of the milk cooler. *Products were placed on storage shelves during the inspection*

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Mashed potatoes, chicken nuggets, and popcorn chicken in the warmer had internal temperatures between 117F & 130F. Final cooking temperatures in log book were noted at 180F/above. Warmer was at the highest setting, but kitchen staff are in/out of the warmer so much it appears the warmer is having a difficult time maintaining foods at 135F/above. All foods are cooked in ovens, on stove top, or in the steamer prior to being portioned on trays and placed in the warmer. Hot potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 135F/above unless a time control policy is in place. A time control policy was established for hot PHF held in the warmer during the inspection (see general comments)

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750.820a - Three part sink was setup improperly. Sinks were setup for wash, sanitize, rinse instead of wash, rinse, sanitize. Sinks were emptied and solutions remade to setup the 3 part sinks to allow for proper manual ware washing. Ware washing process was repeated for equipment/utensils that were recently ran through manual ware washing. For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used properly with the setup being wash, rinse, sanitize and final step of air dry.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Quat test strips were not available for checking sanitizer concentrations. Iodine test strips were found but are not needed. A few test strips were provided by the inspector until Manager could obtain a set from the District 186 Office or Kellner's (deliveries arrive on Wednesdays). A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. **Maintain quat solutions at 200ppm**

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750.820d4 - Equipment/utensils were not being properly sanitized due to improper setup of 3 part sink (see #16 for details). Three part sink was emptied and setup to allow for proper manual ware washing process. Equipment/utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - Large yellow floor fan was observed to have dust buildup on the cover and the blades. Fan was not in use at the time of the inspection. The fan needs to be cleaned and maintained clean if the fan is going to be used in the kitchen. Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and other debris.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Can opener blade had debris stuck on it. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized. Properly wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use utensils and equipment such as serving spoons, can opener, etc. need to be cleaned and sanitized at minimum up to every 4hrs**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Floor drain under 3 part sink was soiled with buildup of debris. Clean the floor drain and the cover daily/as needed and maintain them clean. B) Lower shelving of two plastic shelving units were in direct contact with the floor. Get the shelves adjusted so there is at minimum 6 inches of clearance to adequately clean under the shelves and store food and single service items properly.
